sections.heading: Recognise it
points: Wheeze, cough, breathlessness and chest tightness
Worse at night, with exercise, colds or allergens
Symptoms that come and go, with a personal or family history of atopy

sections.heading: Severity of an attack
points: Moderate: can talk in sentences, SpO2 92% or more
Severe: too breathless to talk or feed, SpO2 under 92%
Life-threatening: silent chest, cyanosis, exhaustion, confusion

sections.heading: Treat an acute attack
points: Salbutamol by spacer, 2 to 10 puffs, repeated every 20 to 30 minutes
Oxygen to keep SpO2 at 94 to 98%

figure.title: First hour of an attack
figure.alt: Give salbutamol by spacer; if improving, continue and give prednisolone; if not, escalate to nebulised treatment and senior review.

nodes.text: Nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium, senior review

sections.heading: Keep it controlled
points: Check inhaler technique and adherence at every visit
A written asthma action plan for home and school

figure.title: Reliever use and control
figure.alt: Children using their reliever three or more times a week are far more often poorly controlled.

takeaway: A child who needs their reliever more than twice a week needs their preventer reviewed.
sources: BTS/SIGN 2019 asthma guideline; NICE NG80; Asthma + Lung UK. Illustrative figures for teaching.
